searchText: I've been playing around with dropping/re-syncing a LH database and I'm getting a scenario where Geth responds to an fcU with `VALID`, but a different head hash to the one I provided. I'm providing it an ancestor of a head I set previously. Looking at the execution spec I don't think that's valid behaviour, but I can see why it might seem like a reasonable thing to do. Looping in <@360491619402776577> FYI I'm sending it an ancient block as the head, about a month old. Hmm does it print something like "ignoring update to previous head"? The spec has the following statement related to the case when head is reset to an older block: > Client software MAY skip an update of the forkchoice state and MUST NOT begin a payload build process if forkchoiceState.headBlockHash doesn't reference a leaf of the block tree ``` INFO [05-11|17:31:06.968] Ignoring beacon update to old head number=226,609 hash=bc3164..aaef78 age=1mo1d6h have=435,272 WARN [05-11|17:31:08.990] Ignoring already known beacon payload number=226,610 hash=8ebe4e..1e6aa3 age=1mo1d6h ``` I think the spec also needs to define a VALID/INVALID/etc for that scenario, since it declares that a VALID response must have `latestValidHash: forkchoiceState.headBlockHash`. Yeah, we return the hash of the head of the canonical chain Even if we ignore the update I think its more correct for us, but if the CL is basing their decisions on us not doing that, we can change it Yeah, I can see why you'd do this. Lighthouse is just having a whinge about it because we think that the spec declares that a `VALID` response *must* include the block hash that we just provided. Basically, spec just says that forkchoice state update may be ignored in this case, it doesn't affect the response at all which should be `status: VALID, lvh: headBlockHash`, but I can understand the source of confusion What is `headBlockHash`, though? What the CL just provided or what the EL has? it's what CL has just provided according to the spec, `forkchoiceState.headBlockHash` -- but it's unclear what `forkchoiceState` does refer to > If validation succeeds, the response MUST contain {status: VALID, latestValidHash: payload.blockHash} This statement is from Payload validation routine, having this logic applied to `fcU` results in `headBlockHash` that CL has provided And I think it's correct, because if CL is syncing and is behind EL's head then CL shouldn't receive block hashes that it isn't familiar with yet Yeah, will change it Looks like a similar thing is happening with `new_payload` too, btw. Old block is supplied but LVH is a newer block. Thats weird, that shouldn't happen imo At prysm we ignore this hash in the VALID case. I can see an use for both cases as sanity checks so I won't advocate nor oppose any specification here, just mentioning that it won't affect us either way TTD has been updated for mainnet-shadow-fork-4, new TTD is `48772237537841292247040` and expected to hit ~2PM UTC (4PM CEST) tomorrow. Configs found here: https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets/tree/main/mainnet-shadow-fork-4

Looping in <@360491619402776577>

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: FYI I'm sending it an ancient block as the head, about a month old.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Hmm does it print something like "ignoring update to previous head"?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
The spec has the following statement related to the case when head is reset to an older block:
> Client software MAY skip an update of the forkchoice state and MUST NOT begin a payload build process if forkchoiceState.headBlockHash doesn't reference a leaf of the block tree

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
```
INFO [05-11|17:31:06.968] Ignoring beacon update to old head       number=226,609 hash=bc3164..aaef78 age=1mo1d6h   have=435,272
WARN [05-11|17:31:08.990] Ignoring already known beacon payload    number=226,610 hash=8ebe4e..1e6aa3 age=1mo1d6h
```

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: I think the spec also needs to define a VALID/INVALID/etc for that scenario, since it declares that a VALID response must have `latestValidHash: forkchoiceState.headBlockHash`.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yeah, we return the hash of the head of the canonical chain

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Even if we ignore the update

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: I think its more correct for us, but if the CL is basing their decisions on us not doing that, we can change it

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Yeah, I can see why you'd do this. Lighthouse is just having a whinge about it because we think that the spec declares that a `VALID` response *must* include the block hash that we just provided.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Basically, spec just says that forkchoice state update may be ignored in this case, it doesn't affect the response at all which should be `status: VALID, lvh: headBlockHash`, but I can understand the source of confusion

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: What is `headBlockHash`, though? What the CL just provided or what the EL has?

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: it's what CL has just provided according to the spec, `forkchoiceState.headBlockHash` -- but it's unclear what `forkchoiceState` does refer to

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
> If validation succeeds, the response MUST contain {status: VALID, latestValidHash: payload.blockHash}
This statement is from Payload validation routine, having this logic applied to `fcU` results in `headBlockHash` that CL has provided

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: And I think it's correct, because if CL is syncing and is behind EL's head then CL shouldn't receive block hashes that it isn't familiar with yet

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yeah, will change it

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: Looks like a similar thing is happening with `new_payload` too, btw. Old block is supplied but LVH is a newer block.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Thats weird, that shouldn't happen imo

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: At prysm we ignore this hash in the VALID case. I can see an use for both cases as sanity checks so I won't advocate nor oppose any specification here, just mentioning that it won't affect us either way
